old: Its root pairs a word for 'self, alone' with a word for 'power.'
It names a system where one person holds all the control.
It shares a root with autokratḗs, Greek for 'one who governs alone.'
clues: This form of government has kept the same core sense since ancient Greek times, built partly from an ancient root meaning 'self, alone.'
It is rule by one person holding absolute, unchecked power. It is broader than dictatorship, which suggests seized control, and unlike monarchy it needn't involve a crown.
Often set against democracy, it describes the tsars' rule in imperial Russia. A related ancient Greek word meant 'one who governs alone.'
